originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq, S&P fall over 1%, end lower for week as chip selloff broadens
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a bad day, with two important groups of stocks, the Nasdaq and S&P, falling by more than 1%. This happened because some technology companies that make computer chips, which are important for artificial intelligence, lost value, making investors nervous. As a result, investors became cautious and sold some of their stocks, which led to a broader decline in the market. Despite some good news from banks, bad forecasts from companies like Netflix made investors less confident. This all added up to a bad week for the stock market.

originalTitle: Reliance Retail Q1 revenue rises, but profit falls as e-commerce weighs
simplifiedContent: Reliance Retail, a big retailer, had an 8.2% increase in sales in the first quarter, which is a good sign. However, the company's profit actually decreased by 14.2% because of the money they're spending on their online shopping business. This decrease in profit is notable, even though sales are up. The company's consumer business, Reliance Consumer, did very well, with sales more than doubling, helped by popular brands like Campa and Independence. This mix of increased sales and decreased profit gives a complex picture of how Reliance Retail is doing.

originalTitle: JSW Steel’s profit doubles on revenue growth, beats estimates
simplifiedContent: JSW Steel, a steel company, made a lot of money in the last quarter, with its profit reaching Rs 4,696 crore, which is more than double what it made last year. This happened because the company sold more products and services, and also because it didn't have to pay as much in interest on its loans. The company's total sales rose by about 10% compared to last year, and its expenses didn't go up as much, which helped increase its earnings. The company's good performance was better than what many people were expecting, which is a positive sign. This news matters because it shows that JSW Steel is doing well financially, which can affect the price of its stock.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble 13% after weak sales forecast, hit 22-month low
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price dropped significantly, by 12.6%, to its lowest point in 22 months. This happened because the company predicted its future sales would be weaker than expected, even though its recent financial results were as anticipated. The reason for the weak sales forecast is that Netflix's revenue growth is slowing down, partly due to issues with its original content and a decrease in its stock value over the past year. This news is important because it shows that Netflix is facing challenges and its stock price is being affected as a result. The drop in stock price means that people who own Netflix shares may see the value of their investment decrease.

originalTitle: Sebi clears automatic SWP, STP mandates for demat mutual fund holdings
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has introduced a new rule that allows automatic transfer of funds from mutual funds held in a demat account. Previously, this automatic feature was only available for mutual fund investments that were not held in a demat account. This change means that investors who hold their mutual funds in a demat account can now set up automatic instructions to transfer funds. This is important because it makes it easier for investors to manage their investments and transfer funds between accounts. This new rule applies to two types of automatic transfer plans: Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plan (STP).

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Earnings sentiment rescues volatile week; real test ahead
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a good week, with two main indexes, the Sensex and Nifty, going up in value. The Sensex rose by 0.75% and the Nifty by 0.53% for the week, with most of the increase happening on Friday. On Friday, the Nifty jumped up by 1.1% and the Sensex by 1.25%, which is a big increase. This is important because it shows that the market is doing well, at least for now, and the Sensex even reached its highest closing level since June 12, 2026. The market's good performance on Friday helped make up for a volatile week, but it's still unclear what will happen next.
